indian.headline: Indian markets fell 0.8–1% today as oil surged past $110, fanning inflation fears.
indian.lead: Indian markets fell 0.8–1% today as oil surged past $110, fanning inflation fears.
indian.brief: Sensex dropped 0.82% and Nifty 50 fell 0.88%, with Bank Nifty sliding 1.01%, as rising crude oil prices and Middle East tensions weighed on sentiment.
why: Oil prices jumped above $110 per barrel due to Middle East tensions, raising inflation worries and pressuring import-dependent sectors like Energy, Auto, and Metals.
Banking stocks fell 1% as higher oil-linked inflation risks could delay interest rate cuts, while IT alone gained 1.8% on relative strength.
Despite Jio Platforms' blockbuster $3.2 billion IPO attracting heavy foreign inflows and pushing the rupee to 94.35, Reliance Industries shares fell 1.5%, offsetting broader momentum.
indian.narrative:
Indian equities opened lower and stayed underwater throughout Thursday, 22 October, with the Sensex shedding 700+ points and Nifty 50 sliding nearly 1%, extending a three-session losing streak. The primary culprit: crude oil prices surged past $110 per barrel on Middle East geopolitical tensions, triggering a cascade of selloffs in oil-sensitive sectors. Energy stocks tumbled 2.4%, Metals fell 2.2%, and Auto slid 2.3% as investors fretted over rising inflation and input costs. Banking, another heavyweight in the indices, sank 1% as higher inflation could force the central bank to hold rates steady longer. FMCG also flagged, down 2%, as margin pressures from costlier crude trickled through supply chains.

Not all news was grim: IT gained 1.8%, buoyed by continued strength in technology exports, while brokerages named Persistent Systems, ONGC, and Godrej Consumer as tactical buy opportunities despite the weakness. Meanwhile, Jio Platforms' record ₹30,213-crore IPO drew a thundering 3.16x subscription in just 100 minutes, channeling heavy foreign capital into the rupee and pushing it to 94.35. Yet Reliance Industries itself sagged 1.5%, a reminder that even the nation's largest company cannot decouple from broad market anxiety over stagflation—a toxic cocktail of stalled growth and rising prices that traders fear may cap rallies for weeks to come.

tiles.label: Global cues
tiles.sub: Middle East tensions pushed crude above $110/bbl, stoking inflation fears globally.

tiles.label: FII activity
tiles.sub: Jio IPO drew heavy foreign inflows, pushing rupee to 94.35 per dollar.

tiles.label: Crude oil
tiles.sub: Oil surged above $110/barrel on Middle East tensions, pressuring Energy and Auto.

indian.watch: Shriram Finance Q2 results (23 Oct) and Jio IPO listing day; monitor oil price holding above $110.

us.headline: US markets mixed as strong earnings offset tech weakness; healthcare and financials lead gains.
us.lead: US markets mixed as strong earnings offset tech weakness; healthcare and financials lead gains.
us.brief: S&P 500 rose 0.28%, Nasdaq fell 0.02%, and Dow jumped 1.02% on mixed sector performance.
why: Healthcare and Financials surged (+2.4% and +1.2%) on strong earnings beats from IBM and optimism around bond valuations, lifting broader market sentiment.
Tech sector declined 0.3% despite Meta's rally, as Netflix shares fell 6% after-hours on weak guidance, signaling investor caution on forward outlooks.
Individual stock moves diverged sharply: General Motors dropped 7% despite beating earnings due to lowered full-year guidance, showing profit quality matters more than just beating estimates.
us.narrative:
US stock markets delivered a mixed performance on October 22, 2026, as strong earnings in healthcare and financials clashed with uncertainty in technology and automaking. The Dow's 1.02% gain outpaced the S&P 500's modest 0.28% rise, while the Nasdaq barely budged at -0.02%. IBM topped expectations with revenue of ₹17.10 billion and profit of $2.95 per share, boosting confidence in the sector. Separately, BlackRock's Rick Rieder flagged high-quality corporate bonds as historically attractive, signaling renewed investor appetite for fixed income.

However, not all earnings cheer proved durable. Netflix shares sank 6% after-hours despite beating profit expectations, as forward guidance disappointed investors—a pattern mirrored by General Motors, which fell 7% despite a strong quarter because it trimmed full-year earnings forecasts. Meta bucked the trend with a stock gain after revealing an AI assistant project (Muse) that could rival its ad business in scale. Meanwhile, in emerging markets, Indonesian stocks fell 2.7% on fears of an MSCI downgrade that could force index fund exclusions. In India, Yash Highvoltage surged 14% on explosive H1 FY27 revenue growth of 95%, while Tech Mahindra announced a 1-for-1 bonus issue on October 15.

tiles.label: Big mover
tiles.sub: H1 FY27 revenue jumped 95% to ₹194.5 crore; net profit up 165%.

tiles.label: Key data
tiles.sub: Adjusted profit of $2.95/share beat expectations; CEO touts AI traction.

tiles.label: Backdrop
tiles.sub: Earnings resilience in healthcare and bonds, but guidance caution in tech and autos.

us.watch: Monitor Netflix and GM earnings follow-up: will guidance misses spark broader sector repricing tomorrow?
